title: 2 Samuel Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 5.

questions.question: Who came to David in Hebron saying, 'Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh'?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 5:1, all the tribes of Israel came to David in Hebron and spoke these words.

questions.question: What did the LORD say to David according to 2 Samuel 5:2?
options: Thou shalt build a temple for me
Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel
Thou shalt conquer all the nations
questions.correctAnswer: Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states that the LORD said to David he shall feed His people Israel and be a captain over Israel.

questions.question: Where did all the elders of Israel anoint David king?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:3 says all the elders of Israel came to David in Hebron and anointed him king over Israel.

questions.question: How old was David when he began to reign?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states David was thirty years old when he began to reign.

questions.question: For how many years did David reign in Hebron over Judah?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:5 records David reigned in Hebron over Judah for seven years and six months.

questions.question: What did the Jebusites say to David when he came to Jerusalem?
options: Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither
You shall be our king forever
questions.correctAnswer: Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states the Jebusites said this to David, thinking he could not enter the city.

questions.question: True or False: David was unable to take the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:7 says David nevertheless took the stronghold of Zion, called the city of David.

questions.question: Who did David say would be chief and captain on that day he smote the Jebusites?
options: Whoever gets up to the gutter and smites the Jebusites, the lame and the blind
questions.correctAnswer: Whoever gets up to the gutter and smites the Jebusites, the lame and the blind
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:8 records David's statement about the chief and captain on that day.

questions.question: True or False: The Jebusites believed that the blind and the lame would come into the house.
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says the Jebusites said the blind and the lame shall not come into the house.

questions.question: What did David call the fort where he dwelt after taking the city?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 5:9, David dwelt in the fort and called it the city of David.

questions.question: What did David build round about from Millo and inward?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 mentions David built round about from Millo and inward, referring to fortifications around the city.

questions.question: True or False: David reigned over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem for thirty and three years.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:5 states David reigned thirty and three years in Jerusalem over all Israel and Judah.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 5, which event happened first?
options: David was anointed king over Israel
David took the stronghold of Zion
David received messengers from Hiram, king of Tyre
questions.correctAnswer: David was anointed king over Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 3 records David's anointing as king before he took the city of David in verse 7 or reigned in Jerusalem in verse 5.

questions.question: Who sent messengers with cedar trees, carpenters, and masons to build David a house?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:11 states Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers and materials to build David a house.

questions.question: True or False: David's kingdom was established and exalted for the sake of Israel's people according to the LORD.
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says David perceived the LORD had established and exalted his kingdom for Israel's sake.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 5:10 show the relationship between David's growth and God's presence?
options: David grew great because the LORD God of hosts was with him
David grew great despite God's absence
David's growth was due to his own strength alone
David's growth was unrelated to God
questions.correctAnswer: David grew great because the LORD God of hosts was with him
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:10 states that David went on and grew great, and the LORD God of hosts was with him, showing that his success was linked to God's presence and blessing.

questions.question: What assistance did Hiram king of Tyre provide to David according to 2 Samuel 5:11?
options: Messengers, cedar trees, carpenters, and masons
questions.correctAnswer: Messengers, cedar trees, carpenters, and masons
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:11 explains that Hiram sent messengers along with cedar trees, carpenters, and masons to build David a house, demonstrating the support given for establishing David’s reign.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 5:12, what realization did David come to about his kingship?
options: The LORD had established him king and exalted his kingdom for Israel's sake
His kingship was due to his military strength alone
He must conquer more lands to prove his rule
His kingdom was fragile and uncertain
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD had established him king and exalted his kingdom for Israel's sake
questions.explanation: David perceived that the LORD had established him king over Israel and exalted his kingdom for the good of the people, highlighting divine providence in his leadership (2 Samuel 5:12).

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 5:13 reveal about David's family life after coming to Jerusalem?
options: He took more concubines and wives and had more sons and daughters
He only had one wife and no children
He sent away all but one wife
questions.correctAnswer: He took more concubines and wives and had more sons and daughters
questions.explanation: Verse 13 states that David took more concubines and wives after coming to Jerusalem, and more children were born to him, indicating the growth of his household.

questions.question: Which of the following names is NOT listed as one of David's sons born in Jerusalem in 2 Samuel 5:14-16?
questions.explanation: The sons listed in verses 14-16 include Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, and several others, but Absalom is not mentioned in this passage as born in Jerusalem.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 5:17, what was David's immediate reaction when he heard the Philistines sought to fight him?
options: He went down to the hold
questions.correctAnswer: He went down to the hold
questions.explanation: Verse 17 explains that upon hearing that the Philistines were coming to seek him, David went down to the hold, indicating a strategic move to prepare for battle.

questions.question: Where did the Philistines position themselves according to 2 Samuel 5:18?
questions.explanation: The Philistines spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim as stated in 2 Samuel 5:18, preparing for battle against David.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 5:19 teach about seeking God's guidance in times of battle?
options: David enquired of the LORD whether to go up against the Philistines and was told to proceed
David ignored God's guidance and attacked anyway
David sought advice only from his generals
questions.correctAnswer: David enquired of the LORD whether to go up against the Philistines and was told to proceed
questions.explanation: David’s inquiry to the LORD and receiving permission to attack (2 Samuel 5:19) demonstrates the importance of seeking divine guidance before action.

questions.question: What name did David give to the place where he defeated the Philistines and why, as described in 2 Samuel 5:20?
options: Baalperazim, because the LORD broke forth upon his enemies like a breach of waters
Geba, because it was a stronghold
Jerusalem, because it was the city of David
questions.correctAnswer: Baalperazim, because the LORD broke forth upon his enemies like a breach of waters
questions.explanation: David named the place Baalperazim to signify the LORD’s powerful victory as a bursting forth of waters against his enemies (2 Samuel 5:20).

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 5:21, what did David and his men do with the images left by the Philistines?
questions.explanation: David and his men burned the images left by the Philistines, showing their rejection of idolatry (2 Samuel 5:21).

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 5:22-24 teach about the importance of obeying God's specific instructions in facing repeated challenges?
options: David was commanded not to attack directly but to circle behind the Philistines and wait for God's sign
David was told to ignore God's advice and fight immediately
God told David to negotiate peace
David was told to retreat and avoid battle
questions.correctAnswer: David was commanded not to attack directly but to circle behind the Philistines and wait for God's sign
questions.explanation: When the Philistines came again, God instructed David to go around them and wait for the sound from the mulberry trees as a signal to attack, emphasizing obedience to God's strategy (2 Samuel 5:22-24).

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 5:25 reveal about the outcome when David obeyed the LORD's command about the Philistines?
options: David successfully smote the Philistines from Geba to Gazer
David was defeated by the Philistines
David made a treaty with the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: David successfully smote the Philistines from Geba to Gazer
questions.explanation: By following the LORD’s instructions, David achieved victory over the Philistines across a wide area (2 Samuel 5:25).

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 5:10-12, David recognized that his success and kingdom were established by his own wisdom and strength.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:10-12 clearly show that David acknowledged the LORD God of hosts was with him and had established his kingdom, not his own wisdom or strength.

questions.question: True or False: Based on 2 Samuel 5:19 and 5:24, David’s victories teach us the importance of seeking and obeying God's guidance before taking action.
questions.explanation: Both verses show David enquiring of the LORD and following His precise instructions, illustrating the blessing of obedience and reliance on God's guidance.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Samuel 5:13-16 teaches that David's family life was static and without growth after moving to Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Verses 13-16 describe David taking more wives and concubines and having many sons born in Jerusalem, indicating growth and change in his family life.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 5.

questions.question: What was the LORD's instruction to David when he inquired about attacking the Philistines the second time?
options: Go up directly and smite them
Do not go up, but come upon them over against the mulberry trees
questions.correctAnswer: Do not go up, but come upon them over against the mulberry trees
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:23 states that the LORD instructed David not to go up directly but to fetch a compass behind them and come upon them opposite the mulberry trees.

questions.question: What name did David give to the place where he first defeated the Philistines after the LORD delivered them into his hand?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 5:20, David named the place Baalperazim because the LORD had broken forth upon his enemies there like a breach of waters.

questions.question: After defeating the Philistines at Baalperazim, what did David and his men do with the Philistine images they found?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:21 reports that David and his men burned the images left by the Philistines after their victory at Baalperazim.

questions.question: What was the significance of the 'sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees' in David's battle strategy?
options: It was a signal to retreat
It indicated the Philistines were fleeing
It was the signal for David to attack
It meant the rain was coming
questions.correctAnswer: It was the signal for David to attack
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:24 explains that when David heard the sound in the mulberry trees, it was the signal to bestir himself because the LORD would go out before him to smite the Philistine host.

questions.question: Which valley did the Philistines spread themselves in during both of their attempts to attack David?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:18 and 5:22 both mention the Philistines spreading themselves in the valley of Rephaim during their attacks against David.

questions.question: How many years did David reign over Judah before he reigned over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:5 states David reigned over Judah in Hebron for seven years and six months before reigning over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does the name 'Baalperazim' mean based on David's declaration after defeating the Philistines?
questions.explanation: David called the place Baalperazim because, as 2 Samuel 5:20 says, the LORD broke forth upon his enemies like the breach of waters, indicating a sudden and overwhelming victory.

questions.question: Which king sent cedar trees, carpenters, and masons to build David a house?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:11 records that Hiram king of Tyre sent materials and workers to build David a house, reflecting political alliance and trade relations.

questions.question: True or False: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for a total of forty years.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:4 clearly states that David was thirty years old when he began to reign and reigned for forty years.

questions.question: True or False: The Jebusites believed David could easily take their city because he was strong and mighty.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:6 shows the Jebusites taunted David, saying he could not enter unless he removed the blind and lame, implying they thought he could not conquer their city.

questions.question: Which literary device is illustrated by David naming the place Baalperazim based on the LORD's action during battle?
questions.explanation: David names Baalperazim after the LORD's 'breaking forth' (2 Samuel 5:20), a form of eponymous naming where a place is named based on an event or characteristic, common in biblical narrative.

questions.question: What Hebrew term translated 'captain' in 2 Samuel 5:2 carries the meaning of a military leader or shepherd of the people?
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 5:2, the term 'captain' comes from the Hebrew 'nagid', which means leader or prince, often used for a military or shepherd-like leader appointed by God.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God going before His people to fight their battles, similar to 2 Samuel 5:24?
questions.explanation: Exodus 14:14 states 'The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace,' echoing the theme in 2 Samuel 5:24 where the LORD goes before David to smite his enemies.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse reflects the concept of Jesus as the Shepherd who leads and delivers his people, resonating with David's role in 2 Samuel 5:2?
questions.explanation: John 10:11 calls Jesus the Good Shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep, paralleling David’s God-appointed role as shepherd and captain of Israel in 2 Samuel 5:2.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 5:25 demonstrate the theme of obedience to God in warfare?
options: David ignored God's commands and won
David consulted his generals instead of God
David followed the LORD's command and smote the Philistines
David used only his own strategy
questions.correctAnswer: David followed the LORD's command and smote the Philistines
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:25 emphasizes David's obedience to God's instructions, leading to victory over the Philistines, underscoring the biblical theme that success comes through divine guidance.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is emphasized by the elders of Israel anointing David king over all Israel in Hebron?
options: The doctrine of election and divine appointment
The separation of church and state
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of election and divine appointment
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:3 shows that David was anointed king before the LORD, demonstrating that his kingship is divinely appointed, which aligns with the doctrine of election and divine appointment.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 5:2, which divine attribute is demonstrated by the LORD appointing David as shepherd and captain over Israel?
questions.explanation: The LORD's declaration that David shall feed His people and be captain over Israel (2 Samuel 5:2) reveals God's sovereignty in choosing and ruling over His people.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth can be drawn from David’s conquest of the Jebusite stronghold, despite the city’s defenses and the enemy’s confidence?
options: The triumph of God’s providential power over human obstacles
The necessity of military might for success
questions.correctAnswer: The triumph of God’s providential power over human obstacles
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:6-7 shows that the Jebusites thought David could not enter their city, but David took it by God’s providential empowerment, illustrating God's power over human opposition.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 5:10 reveal an attribute of God related to David’s success and growth as king?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states the LORD God of hosts was with David, highlighting God’s presence and blessing as the source of David’s growth and success.

questions.question: What redemptive narrative arc is found in the building of David’s house by Hiram king of Tyre as described in 2 Samuel 5:11?
options: The establishment of Israel’s political independence
The foreshadowing of the Messianic kingdom established through David’s lineage
The unity of Israel and Tyre for economic reasons
The end of foreign influence in Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The foreshadowing of the Messianic kingdom established through David’s lineage
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 5:11 records Hiram’s help in building David’s house, which foreshadows the Messianic kingdom promised through David’s line (cf. 2 Samuel 7), a key part of redemptive history.

questions.question: Which doctrinal concept is illustrated by David’s inquiry of the LORD before battle and God’s specific instructions in 2 Samuel 5:19-24?
options: Divine providence and guidance in spiritual warfare
The irrelevance of prayer in warfare
questions.correctAnswer: Divine providence and guidance in spiritual warfare
questions.explanation: David’s seeking the LORD’s guidance and receiving specific battle instructions in verses 19-24 demonstrates divine providence and God’s active guidance in conflict.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by His promise to deliver the Philistines into David’s hands in 2 Samuel 5:19?
questions.explanation: God’s assurance to David that He will deliver the Philistines into his hand (2 Samuel 5:19) reveals God's omnipotent power over enemies.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the success of David was merely due to his military prowess and political alliances. What does 2 Samuel 5:10-11 and 19-25 actually teach about the source of David’s victories?
options: David’s victories were solely due to his military skills
David’s victories were a result of political alliances only
David’s victories were primarily due to divine presence, blessing, and obedience to God’s guidance
David’s victories were accidental and unplanned
questions.correctAnswer: David’s victories were primarily due to divine presence, blessing, and obedience to God’s guidance
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 show God’s presence and blessing with David, and 19-25 demonstrate David’s reliance on God’s guidance in battle, emphasizing divine rather than human factors in his success.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from combining 2 Samuel 5:2 and 5:12 about God’s purpose in establishing David’s kingdom?
options: God establishes kingdoms for political stability only
God’s establishment of David’s kingdom is for the sake of His people Israel and their salvation
God’s kingdom is temporary and limited to David’s lifetime
David’s kingdom was established to replace the priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: God’s establishment of David’s kingdom is for the sake of His people Israel and their salvation
questions.explanation: Verse 2 shows God’s command for David to shepherd Israel, and verse 12 states God exalted David’s kingdom for Israel’s sake, highlighting God’s redemptive purpose in establishing David’s reign.

questions.question: How does the naming of the city of David in 2 Samuel 5:9 reflect a theological theme of God’s kingdom?
options: It symbolizes the eternal city of God
It represents God’s covenant with David and the establishment of His earthly kingdom
It denotes a political alliance with the Jebusites
It signals the end of Israel’s monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: It represents God’s covenant with David and the establishment of His earthly kingdom
questions.explanation: David naming the fortress the city of David (2 Samuel 5:9) symbolizes the establishment of God’s earthly kingdom through David’s reign, central to God’s covenant promises.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do 2 Samuel 5:13-16 and 5:2 convey about the Davidic line and God’s plan of salvation?
options: David’s many children show human frailty and failure
David’s lineage, established by God’s command, foreshadows the Messiah who will shepherd Israel
The number of David's children was a sign of divine disfavor
questions.correctAnswer: David’s lineage, established by God’s command, foreshadows the Messiah who will shepherd Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 13-16 list David’s sons, while verse 2 states God’s command that David shepherd Israel, together pointing to the messianic line through David, key in salvation history.

questions.question: What does David’s burning of the Philistine images in 2 Samuel 5:21 teach about Israel’s understanding of sin and idolatry?
options: Idolatry was tolerated if politically convenient
Idolatry was seen as sinful and a threat to covenant faithfulness
Images were viewed as harmless cultural artifacts
David encouraged syncretism with Philistine religion
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry was seen as sinful and a threat to covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: David and his men burned the Philistine images (2 Samuel 5:21), showing that idolatry was condemned as sin that threatened Israel’s exclusive covenant relationship with God.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 5:14-16 contribute to Christological understanding within the Davidic covenant?
options: It lists David’s sons to show his failure
It highlights Solomon among David’s sons, pointing to the wisdom and future messianic king
It suggests that David’s family was unimportant to God
It denies any messianic significance to David’s lineage
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights Solomon among David’s sons, pointing to the wisdom and future messianic king
questions.explanation: The listing of Solomon among David’s sons (2 Samuel 5:14) points forward to the messianic king, the ultimate fulfillment of the Davidic covenant in Christ.

questions.question: What theological implication arises from David’s alliance with Hiram king of Tyre for building his house (2 Samuel 5:11) in the context of God’s providential rule?
options: God uses Gentile allies to accomplish His purposes
David acted independently without God’s permission
God’s providence is limited to Israel alone
questions.correctAnswer: God uses Gentile allies to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: The cooperation of Hiram king of Tyre in building David’s house (2 Samuel 5:11) shows God’s providential use of Gentiles to fulfill His redemptive plans.

questions.question: What combined theological truth do 2 Samuel 5:17-18 and 5:22-25 teach about the spiritual nature of warfare in David’s time?
options: Warfare was purely political with no spiritual dimension
Spiritual warfare involved reliance on God’s guidance and timing for victory
David’s victories were independent of God’s will
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual warfare involved reliance on God’s guidance and timing for victory
questions.explanation: In these verses, David enquires of the LORD before battle and follows His directions, showing that victory depended on God’s guidance and timing, highlighting the spiritual dimension of warfare.
